shared.text: Ottoline bought the quilt for forty euros.

issues.text: The template says 'a standard that is a clause — taller than Yusra was, older than she looks: no slot here; report the than-phrase as unmapped', but reporting only the than-phrase as unmapped leaves 'Ottoline is taller' with no standard, which cannot be encoded as a comparative without a standard.
issues.sentence: Ottoline is taller than Yusra was.

issues.text: The boundary case 'a standard that is a clause — taller than Yusra was, older than she looks: no slot here; report the than-phrase as unmapped' says to report the than-phrase as unmapped, but the positive property ('is tall') is not entailed and 'comparative' requires 'standard', so the whole comparative clause must be reported as unmapped.
issues.sentence: Ottoline is taller than Yusra was.

issues.text: The boundary case 'a standard that is a clause — taller than Yusra was' instructs to report the than-phrase as unmapped, but the comparative template requires the `standard` slot to be filled, making it impossible to encode the rest of the clause without violating the G01 boundary.
issues.sentence: Ottoline is taller than Yusra was.

issues.text: The 'Unmapped spans' section lists a condition on an individual ('the ladder is brittle when cold') as an example of a whole clause to report as unmapped, whereas the 'conditional' template explicitly covers '<X> is ADJ when / if ADJ' with the example 'Teodor is grumpy when tired'.

The Unmapped spans section lists 'the ladder is brittle when cold' as an example to leave out, contradicting the conditional and conditional-property templates which explicitly specify using the conditional template for 'the ladder is brittle when cold'.
issues.sentence: The ladder is brittle when cold.

issues.text: Intransitive 'swim' with no path or destination could be parsed as `motion` (where 'swim' is an anchor verb) or `activity` (as an action with no change of place).

The comparative template says under 'Not this template' both that a comparison against a bare number such as 'more than 200 metres long' uses the measure template and, in another bullet, to report a comparison with a measure as unmapped.
issues.sentence: The bridge is more than 200 metres long.

issues.text: The modal 'may' on an agentive verb ('Ottoline may leave') is ambiguous between permission (`norm`) and epistemic possibility (`modal`), and the sentence provides no context to decide the reading.
Both psych (agentless passive '<experiencer> was V-ed') and copular (adjectival participle '<subject> was <ADJ>') apply to 'Teodor was frightened'.

Both psych (as an agentless passive `<experiencer> was V-ed` of frighten) and copular (as a past copular predication with the participial adjective frightened) seem to apply to 'Teodor was frightened'.
